from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisites: The Plane and the Cone", [
            "Conic sections arise from slicing a cone.",
            "Imagine a knife cutting through a cone.",
            "Different angles produce unique shapes."
        ])
        
        # --- Create Assets ---
        # Cone wireframe (Using cone parametric surface or simple VGroup)
        # For simplicity and style, we use a simple cone representation
        cone = Cone(base_radius=1.5, height=3, direction=DOWN).rotate(PI/2, axis=RIGHT)
        cone.set_color(BLUE_D)
        
        # Plane
        plane = Square(side_length=3).set_fill(WHITE, opacity=0.3).set_stroke(WHITE, width=1)
        plane.rotate(PI/4, axis=UP)
        
        # Intersection curve
        curve = Ellipse(width=1.5, height=1).set_color(YELLOW)
        
        self.place_in_area(cone, "B2", "E4", scale_factor=0.7)
        self.place_in_area(plane, "B2", "E4", scale_factor=0.7)
        self.place_in_area(curve, "B2", "E4", scale_factor=0.7)
        
        # Initially hide elements
        cone.set_opacity(0)
        plane.set_opacity(0)
        curve.set_opacity(0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(cone), self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(plane), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(curve), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        self.wait(2)

    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Introducing Dandelin Spheres", [

            "They touch the cone in perfect circles.",

        ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Geometry of the Ellipse", [
            "An ellipse forms by slicing one cone.",
            "Points on the ellipse follow specific rules.",
            "The sum of distances is always constant.",
            "Foci are where the spheres touch.",
            "This creates the classic elliptical shape."
        ])
        
        # Ellipse representation
        ellipse = Ellipse(width=3, height=2, color=ORANGE, stroke_width=4)
        self.place_at_grid(ellipse, 'C3')

        # Foci
        f1 = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        f2 = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(f1, 'B2')
        self.place_at_grid(f2, 'D4')

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(ellipse), self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(ORANGE))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(f1), FadeIn(f2), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Point P on ellipse
        p = Dot(color=BLUE)
        p.move_to(ellipse.point_from_proportion(0.2))
        self.add(p)

        # Lines to foci
        l1 = always_redraw(lambda: Line(p.get_center(), f1.get_center(), color=BLUE, stroke_width=2))
        l2 = always_redraw(lambda: Line(p.get_center(), f2.get_center(), color=BLUE, stroke_width=2))
        self.add(l1, l2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.play(MoveAlongPath(p, ellipse), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        foci_label = Text("Foci", font_size=18, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(foci_label, 'B3')
        self.play(Write(foci_label), self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(YELLOW))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(Flash(ellipse, color=ORANGE, num_lines=10), self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(ORANGE))
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Transitions: Parabolas and Hyperbolas", [
            "Changing the plane angle shifts the shape.",
            "Parallel slices create perfect parabolas.",
            "Slicing both cones creates a hyperbola."
        ])
        
        # Mobjects for animations
        cone = Cone(base_radius=1, height=2, color=BLUE).set_opacity(0.5)
        plane = Polygon(LEFT*1, RIGHT*1, UP*0.5, DOWN*0.5, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.3)
        
        self.place_at_grid(cone, 'C2', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(FadeIn(cone))
        self.play(FadeIn(plane))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        # Shift plane to be parallel to side
        self.play(plane.animate.rotate(PI/4, axis=RIGHT).move_to(self.grid['C2']))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        # Tilt further for hyperbola
        self.play(plane.animate.rotate(PI/6, axis=RIGHT).shift(DOWN*0.5))

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Dandelin spheres connect solids to geometry.", "These tangency points are the foci.", "Physics relies on these for planetary orbits."]
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Synthesis", lecture_lines)
        
        # Mobjects for animations
        ellipse = Ellipse(width=2.0, height=1.2, color=BLUE_A)
        parabola = VGroup(
            Axes(x_range=[-1, 1], y_range=[0, 1], x_length=2, y_length=1.2, axis_config={"include_ticks": False}),
            FunctionGraph(lambda x: x**2, x_range=[-1, 1], color=GREEN_A)
        )
        hyperbola = VGroup(
            Axes(x_range=[-1, 1], y_range=[-1, 1], x_length=2, y_length=1.2, axis_config={"include_ticks": False}),
            FunctionGraph(lambda x: 1/x if x != 0 else None, x_range=[0.2, 1], color=RED_A),
            FunctionGraph(lambda x: 1/x if x != 0 else None, x_range=[-1, -0.2], color=RED_A)
        )
        
        # Place them
        self.place_at_grid(ellipse, 'B2')
        self.place_at_grid(parabola, 'B4')
        self.place_at_grid(hyperbola, 'B6')
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE_A), Create(ellipse))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN_A), Create(parabola))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(RED_A), Create(hyperbola))
        
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Fade out
        self.play(FadeOut(self.lecture), FadeOut(ellipse), FadeOut(parabola), FadeOut(hyperbola))
        
        # Final Text
        summary = Text("Dandelin's Principle: From 3D to Planetary Orbits", font_size=32)
        self.play(Write(summary))
        self.wait(3)

outline.topic: The Magic of Dandelin Spheres: Unveiling Conic Sections
outline.target_audience: High school geometry or early undergraduate students

sections.title: Prerequisites: The Plane and the Cone
sections.content: Briefly introduce the 'Double Cone' (a cone extending infinitely in both directions) and a cutting plane. Define the intersection as a conic section. Establish the visual goal: understanding why a slice of a cone results in circles, ellipses, parabolas, or hyperbolas.
sections.example: Imagine a magician slicing a carrot cone with a knife; the angle of the blade determines the shape of the cut.

sections.title: Introducing Dandelin Spheres
sections.content: Introduce the Dandelin Spheres—two spheres placed inside the cone such that they are tangent to both the cone (along a circle) and the cutting plane (at a single point). These points of tangency are the 'Foci' of our conic section.
sections.example: Visualize two glowing bubbles trapped inside a cone, pressed against a flat glass plate, touching it at two specific glowing dots.

sections.title: The Geometry of the Ellipse
sections.content: Demonstrate the Ellipse. Show the plane intersecting only the top half of the cone. Explain that for any point P on the ellipse, the sum of the distances to the two tangency points (foci) is constant—the key definition of an ellipse.
sections.example: A hiker (the point P) trekking on a tilted landscape where the sum of distances to two marked basecamps remains constant.

sections.title: Transitions: Parabolas and Hyperbolas
sections.content: Explain how changing the plane's angle changes the number of spheres trapped. When the plane is parallel to the cone's side (one sphere), it forms a Parabola. When the plane slices both halves (two spheres), it forms a Hyperbola.
sections.example: A satellite dish (Parabola) capturing signals versus a dual-lens telescope (Hyperbola) focusing light from two distinct directions.

sections.title: Summary and Synthesis
sections.content: Recap the beauty of the Dandelin construction: it bridges the gap between 3D solids and 2D geometry. Highlight that the 'magic points' of tangency are the foundation for orbit mechanics in physics.
sections.example: The orbits of planets around the Sun (a focus of the ellipse) are the real-world manifestation of the Dandelin principle in action.
